texts.preamble: Anil Popat Sonawane vs State Of Maharashtra And Anr on 6 March, 2024 Author: Revati Mohite Dere Bench: Revati Mohite Dere 2024:BHC-AS:12034-DBDigitally signed by Nisha Nisha Sandeep Sandeep Chitnis Chitnis Date: 2024.03.13 13:11:36 +0530 In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction Criminal Writ Petition (Stamp) No.3373 Of 2024 Anil Popat Sonawane Age: 32 Years, Occ.: Business, R/o.: Rahu, Tal. Daund, Dist. Pune.
texts.facts: Learned APP waives notice on behalf of respondents-State. 3. By this petition, the petitioner seeks quashing and setting aside of the show-cause-notice dated 22 nd December 2023 issued by the Special Executive Magistrate, Hadapsar Division, Pune City.
texts.arguments: 4. The grievance of the learned counsel for the petitioner is that the show-cause-notice issued under Section 110(a) to (g) is bad in law, inasmuch as, there is nothing to indicate in the said show-cause- notice that the petitioner is a habitual offender, which is a pre- requisite for issuing show-cause-notice under Section 110 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. He submits that reliance is only placed on one C.R. and that too the number of the C.R. is not mentioned in the said show-cause-notice. Section 110 Cr.PC is with respect to 'Security for good behaviour from habitual offenders'. The said Section 110, under which the impugned notice is issued reads as under; "110. Security for good behaviour from habitual offenders.--When an Executive Magistrate receives information that there is within his local jurisdiction a person who-- (a) is by habit a robber, house-breaker, thief, or forger, or (b) is by habit a receiver of stolen property knowing the same to have been stolen, or (c) habitually protects or harbours thieves, or aids in the concealment or disposal of stolen property, or (d) habitually commits, or attempts to commit, or abets the commission of, the offence of kidnapping, abduction, extortion, cheating or mischief, or any offence punishable under Chapter XII of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860), or under section 489-A, section 489-B, section 489-C or section 489-D of that Code, or (e) habitually commits, or attempts to commit, or abets the commission of, offences, involving a breach of the peace, or (f) habitually commits, or attempts to commit, or abets the commission of-- Anil Popat Sonawane vs State Of Maharashtra And Anr on 6 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178353629/ 2 (i) any offence under one or more of the following Acts, namely:- (a) the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 (23 of 1940); (b) the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973 (46 of 1973); (c) the Employees' Provident Funds and Family Pension Fund Act, 1952 (19 of 1952); 903-WPST.3373.2024.doc (d) the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (37 of 1954); (e) the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 (10 of 1955); (f) the Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955 (22 of 1955); (g) the Customs Act, 1962 (52 of 1962); or (h) the Foreigners Act, 1946 (31 of 1946); or (ii) any offence punishable under any other law providing for the prevention of hoarding or profiteering or of adulteration of food or drugs or of corruption, or (g) is so desperate and dangerous as to render his being at large without security hazardous to the community, such Magistrate may, in the manner hereinafter provided, require such person to show cause why he should not be ordered to execute a bond, with sureties, for his good behaviour for such period, not exceeding three years, as the Magistrate thinks fit."
